summary: For a connected reductive group G over a local field F of positive characteristic, Genestier–Lafforgue (and Fargues–Scholze) attach a semisimple parameter L^{ss}(π) to each irreducible representation. The paper proves: (Theorem 1.2) for a discrete series π, L^{ss}(π) has a unique pure Weil–Deligne completion, so tempered representations get essentially tempered L-parameters refining Genestier–Lafforgue (Corollary 1.3); (Theorem 1.4) for F = F_q((t)) with q > 5, G unramified and not a torus, and π compactly induced from a compact open subgroup, L^{ss}(π) is ramified if it is pure, and wildly ramified if the inducing subgroup is sufficiently small; (Theorem 1.5) pure unramified parameters come only from unramified principal series, when supercuspidals of Levi subgroups contain types. The proofs globalise over P^1 by Poincaré series with strict control of ramification at 0 and ∞ (after Gan–Lomelí), a parahoric entry inequality for the matrix entries of parahoric subgroups, Deligne's Weil II and Kummer theory on G_m; Theorem 1.2 uses Sawin–Templier's local purity for irreducible global parameters, Kloosterman representations of Heinloth–Ngô–Yun and, for non-supercuspidal discrete series, Beuzart-Plessis's appendix on the Deligne–Kazhdan simple trace formula. The paper also shows depth-zero generic supercuspidals are pure (conditionally on Dat–Lanard), discusses tempered base change and incorrigible representations, proves for GL(n) that supercuspidals are ramified and either pure or wildly ramified, and conjectures that Genestier–Lafforgue and Fargues–Scholze agree across close local fields. The atlas plans V. Lafforgue's global and Genestier–Lafforgue's local parametrisations (GS.5, GS.7), Weil II weights (DWP.5, DWP.8), buildings and parahorics (RG2.2–RG2.4) and automorphic forms over function fields (FA.6); pending candidates plan Kloosterman sheaves, types, the Ciubotaru–Harris weight constraints and local cyclic base change. Nothing plans tempered refinements of Genestier–Lafforgue parameters, their ramification, the Poincaré-series globalisations or close-field comparisons for general G. Fourteen source issues are recorded; the one of substance is that the orthogonality step (7.7) in the proof of Theorem 7.2 drops the factor −n of (7.5), so the proof of Theorem 1.4(i) is incomplete for k-simple groups that are Weil restrictions from k_n with (q − 1)/gcd(n, q − 1) ≤ 4.

items.name: Theorem 1.2: tempered refinement of the Genestier–Lafforgue parameter of a discrete series
items.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over a local function field F of characteristic p and π an irreducible discrete series representation of G(F). There is a (necessarily unique) essentially tempered L-parameter L(π) : W_F × SL_2 → ^LG whose associated semisimple parameter, L^{ss}(π)(w) = L(π)(w, diag(|w|^{1/2}, |w|^{−1/2})) as in (1.1), is the Genestier–Lafforgue parameter L^{ss}(π).
items.note: Proved for essentially discrete series by Corollary 3.8 with Propositions 3.9 and 3.11.

items.name: Corollary 1.3: a tempered parametrisation refining Genestier–Lafforgue
items.statement: There is a well-defined map L : T(G(F)) → {essentially tempered L-parameters} refining the construction of Genestier–Lafforgue, where T(G(F)) is the set of classes of irreducible essentially tempered representations of G(F).
items.note: Tempered representations are reached from discrete series of Levi subgroups by parabolic induction, with which L^{ss} is compatible (Theorem 2.3(iv)). The paper notes that it does not show L(π) is elliptic for discrete series π.

items.name: Theorem 1.4(i): pure supercuspidal parameters are ramified
items.statement: Let F = k((t)) with k = F_q, q = p^m > 5, and G an unramified connected reductive group over F that is not a torus. Let π be an irreducible supercuspidal representation of the form π ≅ c-Ind_U^{G(F)} τ for a smooth irreducible representation τ, with Q̄_ℓ coefficients, of a compact open (modulo centre) subgroup U. If L^{ss}(π) is pure (for any Frobenius Frob_F, the eigenvalues of L^{ss}(π)(Frob_F) are Weil q-numbers of one weight), then L^{ss}(π) = L(π) is ramified: it is nontrivial on the inertia subgroup I_F.
items.note: The proof of the key step (Theorem 7.2) is incomplete when the k-simple factor of G is not absolutely simple (sourceIssues E1).

items.name: Theorem 1.4(ii): parameters of supercuspidals induced from sufficiently small subgroups are wildly ramified
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 1.4, if U is sufficiently small (Definition 8.2), then L^{ss}(π), and hence L(π), is wildly ramified: nontrivial on the wild inertia subgroup of W_F.

items.name: Theorem 1.5 = Theorem 7.12: pure unramified parameters come from unramified principal series
items.statement: Let F = k((t)) with |k| = q > 5 (a hypothesis the proof needs but the statement omits), G unramified reductive over F and σ an irreducible representation of G(F) whose Genestier–Lafforgue parameter L^{ss}(σ) is pure and unramified. Suppose every supercuspidal representation of every Levi factor of G(F) contains an 𝔰-type, as holds when p ∤ |W_G| (Fintzen) or p is odd and G is an unramified classical group (Stevens). Then σ is an irreducible constituent of an unramified principal series representation of G(F).
items.locator: §1, Theorem 1.5, p. 4; §7.2, Theorem 7.12 and proof, p. 23
items.note: The proof applies Theorems 7.2 and 7.9 (or Corollary 7.11) to the supercuspidal support, which need q > 5; the statement omits it (sourceIssues E2).

items.name: Theorem 2.1(i)–(ii): V. Lafforgue's global parametrisation and twisting
items.statement: (V. Lafforgue, Théorème 0.1) For a global function field K and connected reductive G over K there is a map L : A_0(G) → G^{ss}(G) from cuspidal automorphic representations with central character of finite order to classes of compatible families of semisimple ℓ-adic homomorphisms Gal(K^sep/K) → ^LG, such that at every place v with Π_v unramified, L(Π) is unramified at v and L^{ss}(Π)|_{W_{K_v}} is the Satake parameter of Π_v. For an algebraic character ν : G → G_m and a finite-order Hecke character χ, L(Π ⊗ χ∘ν) = L(Π)·ν̂∘χ̂.
items.note: GS.5 plans V. Lafforgue's excursion construction of global parameters with Satake compatibility (PAPER-LAFFORGUE-18 routes the source there). Printed 'For any Π ∈ 𝒢_0(G)' in (ii) (sourceIssues E4).

items.name: Theorem 2.1(iii) and Theorem 2.3: the Genestier–Lafforgue local parametrisation
items.statement: (Genestier–Lafforgue, Théorème 0.1) For a place v and F = K_v, the semisimplification of L(Π)|_{W_{K_v}} depends only on F and Π_v; this extends to a semisimple parametrisation L^{ss} : A(G, F) → G^{ss}(G, F) of all irreducible admissible representations (2.2), which is (iv) compatible with parabolic induction: if π is a constituent of Ind_{P(F)}^{G(F)} σ, then L^{ss}(π) = i_M ∘ L^{ss}(σ); (v) for quasi-split G, if π^{I(p)} ≠ 0 for the pro-p radical I(p) of an Iwahori subgroup, L^{ss}(π) takes values in ^LT; (vi) compatible with homomorphisms Υ : G_1 → G_2 with normal image (in particular isogenies of semisimple groups): L^{ss}(π ∘ Υ) = ^LΥ ∘ L^{ss}(π), and likewise globally ([Laf18, Prop. 12.5]).
items.note: PAPER-LAFFORGUE-18 marked the Genestier–Lafforgue parametrisation and its local–global compatibility as planned in GS.7 (with GS.4); PAPER-FENG-24 routed its use through the Bernstein centre to its own Part II. For (vi) the restriction π ∘ Υ need not be irreducible; the statement is meant for its constituents.

items.name: Corollary 2.4: parameters as symmetric monoidal functors
items.statement: (i) For Π ∈ A_0(G) unramified outside |X|, τ ↦ V(Π, τ) := τ ∘ L(Π) is a symmetric monoidal functor from Rep(^LG) to completely reducible local systems on Y ∖ |X|. (ii) Likewise τ ↦ L^{ss}(σ, τ) := τ ∘ L^{ss}(σ) for σ ∈ A(G, F), to completely reducible representations of W_F. (iii) If V(Π, τ) is abelian and semisimple for some faithful τ, the image of L(Π) meets Ĝ inside a maximal torus.
items.note: The standard Tannakian description of Ĝ-local systems (Simpson, p. 52).

items.name: Definition 2.5: pure representations
items.statement: σ ∈ A(G, F) is pure if for some (equivalently every) faithful τ : ^LG → GL(N) and any Frobenius element Frob_F ∈ W_F, the eigenvalues of L^{ss}(σ, τ)(Frob_F) are Weil q-numbers of a single weight.

items.name: Definition 3.1 and the Gross–Reeder dictionary: Weil–Deligne parameters and L-parameters
items.statement: A Weil–Deligne parameter for F with values in ^LG(C) is a pair (ρ, N) of a continuous ρ : W_F → ^LG(C) (discrete topology on C) and a nilpotent N ∈ Lie(Ĝ)(C) such that (Ad ∘ ρ, N) is a homomorphism from the Weil–Deligne group to Aut(Lie Ĝ)(C). Gross–Reeder [GR, §2.1, Prop. 2.2] give an equivalence between such pairs and L-parameters φ_{ρ,N} : W_F × SL(2, C) → ^LG(C), algebraic on the second factor.
items.note: LP0 owns L-parameters of W_E valued in the L-group as continuous cocycles; this adds the monodromy operator and the SL_2 form. PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23-B routed Φ(G) with component groups (for G_2) to ExceptionalThetaCorrespondencesForG2; the general definition belongs here.

items.name: Definition 3.2: tempered and essentially tempered parameters
items.statement: (ρ, N) is tempered if the restriction of φ_{ρ,N} to W_F × SU(2) has bounded image after projection to Ĝ(C), and essentially tempered if its image in Ĝ^{ad} is bounded.

items.name: Definition 3.3: pure Weil–Deligne parameters
items.statement: (a) A Weil–Deligne representation (ρ, N) on V is pure if there is t ∈ C such that (i) the eigenvalues of ρ_t(Frob_F) := ρ(Frob_F)q^t are q-numbers of integer weight; (ii) the subspace W_aV of (generalised) eigenvectors of ρ_t(Frob_F) with eigenvalues of weight ≤ a is (ρ, N)-stable; (iii) there is an integer w (the weight) with N^i : gr_{w+i}V → gr_{w−i}V an isomorphism for all i ≥ 0. (b) A parameter valued in ^LG(C) is pure if (σ ∘ ρ, N) is pure of some weight for some (equivalently every) faithful representation σ of ^LG. For N = 0 this is purity of the Weil parameter (Taylor–Yoshida's 'strictly pure'). Remark 3.4: for ℓ-adic parameters, ι-purity after an isomorphism ι : Q̄_ℓ ≅ C.
items.note: Printed with N for N^i in (iii) (sourceIssues E3). DWP.5 plans pure Weil–Deligne representations and the monodromy filtration (PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26 marks the same definition planned there); (b) composes with a faithful representation.

items.name: Lemma 3.5: purity versus temperedness, and uniqueness of the pure completion
items.statement: (a) (ρ, N) is pure if and only if φ_{ρ,N} is essentially tempered. (b) A semisimple parameter ρ : W_F → ^LG(C) has at most one completion, up to equivalence, to a pure Weil–Deligne parameter (ρ, N) (its pure completion); equivalently, at most one essentially tempered L-parameter has ρ as its semisimple parameter via (1.1).
items.note: For GL(n) this is [TY, Lemma 1.4(3)–(4)]; for general G the proof follows Arthur [A84, p. 10]: the restriction of φ_{ρ,N} to SL(2) is unique up to conjugacy in the reductive centraliser of φ|_{W_F}.

items.name: Lemma 3.6 (Sawin–Templier): local purity of irreducible global parameters
items.statement: (Sawin–Templier, [ST, Lemma 11.4]) Let X be a smooth projective curve over a finite field with K = k(X) and ρ : Gal(K^sep/K) → ^LG(C) irreducible (its image lies in no proper parabolic subgroup, parabolic subgroups defined dynamically via cocharacters λ : G_m → ^LG). For every place z, the Weil–Deligne parameter (ρ_z^{ss}, N_z) of the restriction ρ_z to a decomposition group at z is pure.
items.note: [ST] states it for split semisimple G; Remark 3.7 extends it to reductive G. The deduction uses the mixedness from L. Lafforgue and Weil II, Theorem 1.8.4 and Proposition 1.6.13.

items.name: Weil II: the monodromy weight filtration and extension of pure local systems
items.statement: (Deligne, Weil II, Theorem 1.8.4, Proposition 1.6.13, Corollary 1.7.6) For a pure lisse sheaf on an open curve, the i-th graded piece of the local monodromy filtration at a missing point is pure of weight w + i. If at every z ∈ Z (Z nonempty) the semisimplified local monodromy ρ_z^{ss} is unramified and the Frobenius eigenvalues ρ_z(Frob_z) are Weil q-numbers of one weight, the local system extends over Z (Theorem 4.2).
items.note: DWP.5 plans the local weight theorem for pure lisse sheaves on curves, including the weights of the monodromy graded pieces; DWP.8 the weight filtrations.

items.name: Corollary 3.8: pure completions from irreducible globalisations
items.statement: Let π be an irreducible admissible representation of G(F). Suppose X is a smooth projective curve over a finite field, z a place of K = k(X) with K_z ≅ F, and Π a cuspidal automorphic representation of G_K with Π_z ≅ π whose global parameter L(Π) is irreducible. Then the Weil–Deligne parameter L_Π(π) = (L^{ss}(π), N_Π) of L(Π)|_{Γ_z} is pure, and it is the unique pure completion of L^{ss}(π).

items.name: Proposition 3.9: irreducible globalisations of supercuspidals
items.statement: Let π be a supercuspidal representation of G(F), X a smooth projective curve over a finite field and z a place of K = k(X) with K_z ≅ F. There are infinitely many cuspidal automorphic representations Π of G_K with Π_z ≅ π and L(Π) irreducible. In particular L^{ss}(π) has a pure completion realised as the specialisation at z of L(Π).
items.note: Proof: choose x ≠ z with G(K_x) split, a supercuspidal π′ of G(K_x) with L^{ss}(π′) irreducible (the local component at ∞ of the Kloosterman representation π(φ, χ) of Heinloth–Ngô–Yun), and a Poincaré series with Π_x ≅ π′, Π_z ≅ π and tame elsewhere ([GLo]).

items.name: Kloosterman sheaves and the irreducibility of their monodromy at ∞
items.statement: (Heinloth–Ngô–Yun, Theorem 2; Xu–Zhu, Cor. 4.5.8, Rem. 4.5.10) For split G over k′ the Kloosterman sheaf Kl_Ĝ(φ, χ) on P^1_{k′} ∖ {0, ∞} is the global parameter (Remark 3.10: by Chebotarev and Satake compatibility) of an automorphic representation π(φ, χ) (made explicit by Yun), and the restriction of its local monodromy at ∞ to the inertia group is irreducible, with no restriction on p when G(K_x) is split; hence L^{ss}(π′) is irreducible for the local component π′ of π(φ, χ) at ∞, even after composing with the adjoint representation.
items.locator: §3.3, proof of Proposition 3.9 and Remark 3.10, pp. 10–11
items.note: KloostermanSheavesAndBesselIsocrystals (proposed by PAPER-XU-ZHU-22) plans Kl_Ǧ, its local monodromy at ∞ and the removal of HNY's restrictions on p.

items.name: Gan–Lomelí: globalisation of supercuspidals over function fields by Poincaré series
items.statement: (Gan–Lomelí, JEMS 20 (2018)) For supercuspidal representations π_i at finitely many places of a global function field, there is a cuspidal automorphic representation Π with these local components and tame (or unramified) components elsewhere, constructed as a constituent of a Poincaré series P_φ(g) = Σ_{γ∈G(K)} φ(γg) built from matrix coefficients supported on compact open subgroups; the series converges absolutely, and P_φ(1) ≠ 0 when the support meets G(K) only in the identity (or in a controlled finite group).
items.note: The method of the whole paper; §§6–8 and 9.3 refine it with precise control at 0 and ∞.

items.name: Proposition 3.11: irreducible globalisations of discrete series up to cuspidal support
items.statement: Let π be an essentially discrete series representation of G(F), with X, z as in Proposition 3.9. There is a cuspidal automorphic representation Π of G_K with L^{ss}(Π_z) = L^{ss}(π) and L(Π) irreducible; so L^{ss}(π) has a pure completion L(π), the specialisation at z of L(Π).
items.note: Proof: a pseudo-coefficient f_π and Lemma A.1 give Π with Π_x ≅ π′ and Tr(Π_z)(f_π) ≠ 0, so Π_z has the cuspidal support of π ([GLo, Lemma 8.1]).

items.name: Corollary 3.12: the adjoint parameter of a discrete series is pure of weight 0
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.2 with G semisimple, Ad ∘ L(π) is pure of weight 0. Remark 3.13: L(π) is ι-pure for every ι.
items.note: Ad ∘ L(π) is pure of some weight w and its determinant has weight 0, so w = 0.

items.name: Corollary 4.3: tame local systems on G_m split into rank-one systems
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 4.2 with X = {0, ∞}, let V be a semisimple local system on Y = P^1 ∖ (X ∪ Z) whose local monodromy at 0 and ∞ is tame and whose semisimplified local monodromy at 0 or ∞ is abelian and Frobenius-semisimple. Then, after a finite extension of the coefficient field, V is a sum of rank-one local systems.
items.note: Uses L. Lafforgue [Laf02, Cor. VII.8] to write a tame local system on G_m as ⊕_χ V_χ ⊗ χ with V_χ mixed.

items.name: L. Lafforgue: decomposition of local systems into mixed ones up to constant twists
items.statement: (L. Lafforgue, [Laf02, Cor. VII.8]) A local system V on a curve over k can be written as a finite direct sum ⊕_χ V_χ ⊗ χ, with each V_χ mixed and χ the pullback of a continuous ℓ-adic character of Gal(k̄/k).
items.note: A consequence of L. Lafforgue's correspondence for GL_n and Deligne's conjecture (i), which GS.6 plans.

items.name: Kummer theory for K = k(t) and for k
items.statement: K′ is the union of abelian extensions of K of degree dividing q − 1, and ψ : K^×/(K^×)^{q−1} ≅ X(K) = Hom(Gal(K′/K), Q̄_ℓ^×) (4.4); C_T ⊂ K^×/(K^×)^{q−1} is generated by k^× and T, X_T = ψ(C_T); similarly ψ_k : k^× ≅ X(k) = Hom(Gal(k′/k), Q̄_ℓ^×) (4.5) for the cyclic extension k′ of degree q − 1 (with q^{q−1} elements), with β^b := ψ_k(b)(β). Elements α ∈ X_T are unramified at z ∈ G_m(k) and define α^{(z)} : Γ_z/I_z ≅ Gal(k′/k) → Q̄_ℓ^×; α_a := ψ(T^a).

items.name: Lemma 4.6: a reciprocity law for Kummer characters
items.statement: For z ∈ G_m(k) and a = 1, …, q − 1: (α_a)^{(z)} = ψ_k(z^a).
items.note: Printed ψ_k(az) (sourceIssues E5).

items.name: Lemma 4.7: Frobenius traces of rank-one local systems on G_m
items.statement: For a rank-one local system L on G_{m,k} and z ∈ k^×: tr(Frob_z, L) = tr(Frob_1, L)·tr(m_z^{−1}, L), where m_z ∈ I_0 multiplies the (q − 1)st root of T by z.
items.note: Two proofs: global class field theory for K (the idèle (T − z)/(T − 1)) and Kummer theory with Lemma 4.6.

items.name: Class field theory and Chebotarev density for global function fields
items.statement: Global class field theory for K = k(t) (the tame abelianised fundamental group of G_m as a quotient of the idèle class group), and Chebotarev density for ℓ-adic local systems.
items.locator: §3.3, Remark 3.10, p. 11; §4.2, proof of Lemma 4.7, p. 14
items.note: FA.4 plans global class field theory and FA.5 Chebotarev.

items.name: Bruhat–Tits buildings, parahoric and Moy–Prasad subgroups of unramified groups
items.statement: For an unramified group G over K (quasi-split, split by an unramified extension, hence defined over k) with Borel B = TN, maximal k-split torus S ⊂ T, faithful representation ρ : G → Aut(V) with S-eigenbasis e_i of weights λ_i: at each place y, G(O_y) is hyperspecial; the preimage I_y of B(k_y) is an Iwahori subgroup with pro-p radical I(p) the preimage of N(k_y); the apartment A(A_y) ≅ X_*(A_y) ⊗ R with G(O_y) the stabiliser of 0, and for y ∈ P^1(k), A_y = S_y and the apartments are identified with X_*(S) ⊗ R; parahoric subgroups G_c for points c of the apartment are generated by the affine root subgroups U_ψ with ψ(c) ≥ 0, and Moy–Prasad subgroups G_{c,r+} by the U_ψ with ψ(c) > r and the tori T^a_{nδ}, n > r.
items.note: RG2.2 plans buildings and the group action, RG2.3 parahoric and congruence group schemes, RG2.4 the Iwahori and Cartan decompositions.

items.name: Lemma 5.1: the parahoric entry inequality
items.statement: Let F = k((t)), G an unramified semisimple group with maximal F-split torus S in a Borel B = TN, all defined over k; c a point of the apartment of S with parahoric G_c; ρ : G → Aut(V) faithful over k with S-eigenbasis e_1, …, e_n of weights λ_i. For g ∈ G_c: v(ρ_{ij}(g)) ≥ c·(λ_i − λ_j) (5.2). If g ∈ G_{c,r+} with r ≥ 0: v(ρ_{ij}(g) − δ_{ij}) > c·(λ_i − λ_j) + r (5.3).
items.note: Proof on generators: on a root group U_b, ρ_{ij} vanishes unless λ_i − λ_j = nb (n ≥ 0) and is homogeneous of degree n, checked by lifting to W(k) and SL_2 theory.

items.name: Proposition 6.1: a compact open subgroup meeting G(K) in T(k)
items.statement: Let G be unramified and simply connected over K = k(t), U* ⊂ G(F) a fixed maximal compact subgroup, and U = ∏_x U_x with U_z = U* (via G(K_z) ≅ G(F)) for z ∈ G_m(k), U_x = G(O_x) for x ∉ P^1(k), and U_0, U_∞ parahoric. U_0 and U_∞ can be chosen (as G_a and G_b with a + b + (q − 1)c = 0 and a generic) so that G(K) ∩ U = T(k).
items.note: The product formula with Lemma 5.1 forces equality in (5.2) at every place.

items.name: Corollary 6.2 and Remark 6.3: trivial intersection with pro-p Iwahori level
items.statement: Under Proposition 6.1 one can choose Iwahori subgroups I_0 ⊂ U_0 and I_∞ ⊂ U_∞ with G(K) ∩ (∏_{x≠0,∞} U_x × I_∞(p) × I_0) = {1}. If U_z = G(O_z) for z ∈ G_m(k), one can take U_0 = I^+ and U_∞ = I^− (upper and lower Iwahori subgroups), and then G(K) ∩ U = T(k), since G(K) ∩ ∏_x G(O_x) = G(k).

items.name: Theorem 7.1: purity implies ramification modulo the centre
items.statement: Let F = k((t)), k = F_q, q > 5, G unramified connected reductive over F and not a torus, and π ≅ c-Ind_U^{G(F)} τ supercuspidal with U compact open modulo centre. If L^{ss}(π) is pure then f ∘ L^{ss}(π) = f ∘ L(π) is ramified, where f : ^LG → ^LG/Z(Ĝ). By Theorem 2.3(vi) applied to G_sc → G_der → G it suffices to treat G k-simple and simply connected.

items.name: The Frobenius-invariant character α
items.statement: For G unramified, simply connected and k-simple over k: the adjoint representation of Ĝ is a sum of irreducibles 𝔳_1, …, 𝔳_n, one for each simple factor of G_k̄, permuted transitively by W_k; α̂_i, the highest weight of 𝔳_i, is a coroot of G with root α_i, and α = Σ_i α_i ∈ X^*(T) is W_k-invariant.
items.note: Printed 'the action of W_i' for W_k (sourceIssues E6).

items.name: DeBacker–Reeder: tame characters of T(k) and tame parameters
items.statement: (DeBacker–Reeder, §4.3) For an unramified torus T over k split over k_n = F_{q^n}: Hom(T(k), Q̄_ℓ^×) ≅ Hom_Frob(I_t, T̂) ≅ Hom_Frob(k_n^×, T̂), with I_t the tame inertia group; hence the restriction to inertia of the parameter of a depth-zero character χ of T(F) is determined by, and determines, χ|_{T(k)}.

items.name: Theorem 7.2: a globalisation with prescribed tame data forces ramification
items.statement: Let F = k((t)), k = F_q, q > 5, G unramified simply connected k-simple, σ supercuspidal of G(F), K = k(P^1). Suppose Π is a cuspidal automorphic representation of G(A_K) with (a) Π_z ≅ σ for every z ∈ G_m(k); (b) Π_∞ has nonzero I_∞(p)-invariants; (c) Π_0 is a constituent of Ind_{B(F)}^{G(F)} χ with χ tame and χ|_{T(k)} = μ ∘ α for a faithful character μ of k^×; (d) Π_y is G(O_y)-unramified for y ∉ P^1(k). Then L^{ss}(σ) pure ⇒ L^{ss}(σ) ramified.
items.note: Proof: if L^{ss}(σ) were unramified, the tensor-induced local system V(Π, ⊗𝔳_i) extends to G_m (Theorem 4.2), each V(Π, 𝔳_i) splits into rank-one systems over k_n (Corollary 4.3), and Lemma 4.7 with orthogonality of characters of k^× isolates the highest-root term. The orthogonality step (7.7) drops the factor −n of (7.5); the argument is complete for n = 1 but not in general (sourceIssues E1).

items.name: 𝔰-types
items.statement: A supercuspidal σ of G(F) contains an 𝔰-type if σ ≅ c-Ind_{U*}^{G(F)} ρ (7.8) for an open compact subgroup U* and an irreducible representation ρ of U*; then σ has a matrix coefficient φ* supported in U* with φ*(1) = 1.

items.name: Theorem 7.9: Poincaré series with the data of Theorem 7.2
items.statement: Let K = k(P^1), F = k((t)) and σ a supercuspidal representation of G(F) (G semisimple simply connected) containing an 𝔰-type (U*, ρ). Then there is a cuspidal automorphic representation Π of G(A_K) satisfying (a)–(d) of Theorem 7.2.
items.note: The Poincaré series of φ = ∏ φ_x (φ* at z ∈ G_m(k), 1_{I_∞(p)} at ∞, χ_k on I_0, 1_{G(O_x)} elsewhere) has P_φ(1) = 1 by Corollary 6.2.

items.name: Fintzen and Stevens: supercuspidals contain 𝔰-types
items.statement: (Fintzen, Ann. Math. 193 (2021)) If p does not divide |W_G|, every supercuspidal representation of G(F) is compactly induced from an open compact (modulo centre) subgroup. (Stevens, Invent. Math. 172 (2008)) For p odd and G a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, the same holds.
items.locator: §1, p. 3; §7.2, Corollary 7.11, Theorem 7.12, pp. 22–23; §10.1, Proposition 10.5, p. 30
items.note: SmoothRepresentationsPartII (proposed by PAPER-FINTZEN-21 and PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17) plans Fintzen's types; Stevens' classical-group types are not yet in its brief.

items.name: Corollary 7.11: Theorem 1.4(i) when p ∤ |W|
items.statement: Let G be unramified reductive over a local field F of characteristic p with constant field of order q > 5, not a torus, with p ∤ |W_G|. If σ is pure, f ∘ L^{ss}(σ) is ramified. In particular Theorem 1.4(i) holds.

items.name: Theorem 8.1: wild ramification for sufficiently small inducing subgroups
items.statement: Let G be unramified over F = k((t)), J an open subgroup of a parahoric G_a and σ a representation of J with π = c-Ind_J^{G(F)} σ irreducible. If J is sufficiently small and q > 5, then f ∘ L^{ss}(π), hence f ∘ L(π), is wildly ramified.
items.note: Proof: two Poincaré series Π_1, Π_2 unramified outside {0, ∞}, both ≅ π at 0 but with Iwahori-fixed vectors at ∞ for Π_1 and not for Π_2; if L^{ss}(π) were tame, the tame fundamental group of G_m would force their tame inertia at ∞ to agree.

items.name: Definition 8.2: sufficiently small subgroups
items.statement: (i) A finite subgroup H ⊂ G(k) is sufficiently small if B(k) ∩ H = {1} for some Borel k-subgroup B. (ii) J ⊆ G_a is sufficiently small if its image in G_a/G_{a,0+} is. Examples: the unipotent radical of a Borel subgroup (by the Bruhat decomposition), and G_{a,0+}.

items.name: Lemma 8.3: a compact open subgroup whose rational points lie in a Borel
items.statement: For a ∈ A(S_0) and b a small perturbation of −a in A(S_∞) with a + b a small rational multiple of a regular dominant cocharacter, and C = ∏_v G_{f(v)} (f(0) = a, f(∞) = b, f = 0 elsewhere), the map C ∩ G(K) → C_0 → G_a → G_a/G_{a,0+} is injective with image in a Borel subgroup of G_a/G_{a,0+}.
items.note: Printed with 'Lemma 5.1(ii)' for (5.3) and G_{0,a+} for G_{a,0+} (sourceIssues E7).

items.name: Poincaré series II
items.statement: With C′ = J × ∏_{v≠0} C_v (after conjugating J so that J ∩ B_λ = {1}), C′ ∩ G(K) = {1}. For a nontrivial character χ of the torus G_b/G_{b,0+} (q > 2), Poincaré series built from matrix coefficients of σ and of σ ⊗ χ give cuspidal Π_1, Π_2 unramified outside {0, ∞}, with Π_{1,0} ≅ Π_{2,0} ≅ π, Π_{1,∞} having Iwahori-fixed vectors and Π_{2,∞} not.

items.name: Proposition 8.5: a special case by Theorem 7.2
items.statement: If G_a is hyperspecial, J ⊆ G_{a,0+} and π = c-Ind_J σ is a pure supercuspidal representation of G(F), then L^{ss}(π) is wildly ramified.
items.note: Printed 'Under the hypotheses of Proposition 8.1' and 'of G(K)' (sourceIssues E8). A Poincaré series unramified away from ∞ has a parameter tame at ∞ only if unramified there, since the tame fundamental group of A^1 is trivial.

items.name: Proposition 9.1: globally generic globalisation of depth-zero generic supercuspidals
items.statement: Let G be unramified semisimple over k and π ≅ c-Ind_{G(O_F)}^{G(F)} σ a depth-zero generic supercuspidal representation, with σ a generic cuspidal representation of G(k). There is a globally generic cuspidal Π of G over K = k(t) with Π_0 ≅ π, Π_∞ ≅ π^∨ and Π_v G(O_v)-unramified at all other places.
items.note: The Poincaré series of f_0(g) = ⟨σ(g)w, w⟩ on G(O_0) and f_∞(g) = ⟨w, σ(g)w⟩ on G(O_∞), for a ψ-Whittaker vector w, has P_f(1) = Σ_{γ∈G(k)} |⟨σ(γ)w, w⟩|² ≠ 0 and a nonzero (N, Ψ)-Whittaker coefficient.

items.name: Expected Theorem 9.3 (Dat–Lanard): depth-zero parameters are tame
items.statement: (Dat–Lanard, conditional on the ℓ-independence of L^{ss}(π)) For a depth-zero supercuspidal π ∈ A(G, F) (in the sense of DeBacker–Reeder), L^{ss}(π) is at most tamely ramified.
items.note: Footnote 3: the latest version of [DL] (April 2024) refers to an announcement that Scholze has proved the independence of ℓ.

items.name: Ciubotaru–Harris: generic unitary unramified components have no widely separated integral weights
items.statement: (Ciubotaru–Harris, [CH], main theorem, as used) For a cuspidal globally generic automorphic representation Π of G over a function field, the Satake parameter of an unramified local component Π_z (unitary and generic) cannot have two integral weights differing by at least 2.
items.note: GlobalShtukasPartIIRamanujanArthur (proposed by PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26) plans the generic function-field temperedness theorem ('generic-global-theorem').

items.name: Theorem 9.4: depth-zero generic supercuspidals are pure (conditionally)
items.statement: Assume G semisimple over k and p a good prime for G. Then for any depth-zero generic supercuspidal representation π of G(F), L^{ss}(π) is pure.
items.note: Proved using Expected Theorem 9.3, which [DL] establish only conditionally on the independence of ℓ (§9.2 says so); with Proposition 9.1, Theorem 1.2, Corollary 3.12 and [CH].

items.name: Definition 10.1: tempered base change
items.statement: G (over E = k((t))) admits tempered base change if for every pair F ⊂ F′ of finite extensions of E with F′/F cyclic of prime order there is a map BC_{F′/F} : T(G, F) → P(T(G, F′)) (nonempty sets of tempered representations) with L^{ss}_{F′}(π′) = L^{ss}_F(π)|_{W_{F′}} (10.2) for every π′ ∈ BC_{F′/F}(π).

items.name: Definition 10.3: incorrigible supercuspidal representations
items.statement: If G admits tempered base change, a supercuspidal π of G(F) is incorrigible if for every tower F = F_0 ⊂ F_1 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ F_r of cyclic extensions of prime order (10.4), the iterated base change BC_{F_r/F}(π) contains a supercuspidal member.
items.note: After Harris, 'Incorrigible representations' (arXiv:1811.05050).

items.name: Proposition 10.5: pure supercuspidals are not incorrigible
items.statement: Assume G admits tempered base change and p ∤ |W|, or more generally that every supercuspidal representation of every Levi subgroup of G(F) contains an 𝔰-type. Then for any extension F/E no pure supercuspidal representation of G(F) is incorrigible.
items.note: The proof cites 'Corollary 7.12' for Theorem 7.12 (sourceIssues E9); the tower can be chosen to make L^{ss} unramified and the residue field large.

items.name: Labesse: cyclic base change for p-adic groups by the stable twisted trace formula
items.statement: (Labesse, Astérisque 257) For a supercuspidal π with central character of finite order of G(F), F p-adic, globalised at a place w of a totally real K with compact-modulo-centre archimedean components and Steinberg components at chosen places, and a totally real cyclic K′/K, there is a nonempty collection of automorphic Π′ of G_{K′} which are the unramified base change of Π at every place where Π and K′/K are unramified; BC(π) is the set of the Π′_w.
items.note: ML.5 registers cyclic base change among the known transfers with their exact hypotheses. The stabilisation it needs is now available (Mœglin–Waldspurger; Clozel–Harris–Labesse–Ngô).

items.name: Böckle–Feng–Harris–Khare–Thorne and Henniart–Lemaire: cyclic base change over local function fields
items.statement: (Böckle–Feng–Harris–Khare–Thorne, [BFHKT, Thm. 7.2]) For π as in Theorems 7.1 and 7.2 there is c(π) such that for every cyclic F′/F of prime degree m > c(π) there is π′ of G(F′) with L^{ss}(π′) = L^{ss}(π)|_{W_{F′}}. (Henniart–Lemaire, Mém. SMF 124 (2011)) GL(n) over a local function field admits tempered base change, with BC_{F′/F}(π) a singleton.
items.note: [BFHKT] was a 2022 manuscript when cited. ModPBernsteinCentersAndLocalBaseChange (proposed by PAPER-FENG-24) plans local cyclic base change for Genestier–Lafforgue parameters.

items.name: §10.3: the base-change alternative for small residue fields
items.statement: Let π be a supercuspidal as in Theorems 7.1–7.2 and π_m its base change to the unramified F′ of prime degree m > c(π) (residue field of order q^m). Then L^{ss}(π) is unramified iff L^{ss}(π_m) is, and either (i) for some m ≥ sup(3, c(π)), π_m is supercuspidal, and Theorems 7.1 and 7.2 hold for π with no hypothesis on q, or (ii) for all m ≥ sup(3, c(π)), π_m is not supercuspidal.
items.note: The paper calls (ii) 'clearly absurd' but cannot exclude it.

items.name: Bushnell–Kutzko: supercuspidals of GL_n are induced from simple types
items.statement: (Bushnell–Kutzko, Theorem 8.4.1, Definitions 1.4.3–1.5.5, 3.1.8, 5.5.10) Every supercuspidal π of GL(n, F) contains a simple type (J, λ). In case (a), attached to a simple stratum [𝔄, n, 0, β] (𝔄 principal hereditary, E = F[β] with E^× normalising 𝔄, v_𝔄(β) = −n, 0 < −k_0(β, 𝔄)), π = Ind(Λ) for a representation Λ of E^×J(β, 𝔄), with J(β, 𝔄) = 𝔍(β) ∩ 𝔄^× and 𝔍(β) ⊆ 𝔅 + 𝔓; in the other case π = Ind(Λ) for Λ a representation of F^×U(𝔄). Units of E^× lie in 𝔄^× (Prop. 1.2.1), and a principal hereditary order is, in a suitable basis, block upper triangular modulo 𝔭_F with e × e blocks.
items.locator: §10.4, proof of Lemma 10.6 and before Lemma 10.8, pp. 32–33
items.note: SmoothRepresentationsPartII (PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17's addition) plans hereditary orders, simple strata and the BK simple-character construction.

items.name: Lemma 10.6: two shapes of supercuspidals of GL_n
items.statement: Let π be a supercuspidal representation of GL(n, F). Either (a) there are a principal hereditary order 𝔄 ⊂ M_n(F) and a field E ⊂ M_n(F), [E : F] > 1, with E^× normalising 𝔄, and a representation Λ of E^×·(𝔄^× ∩ (𝔅 + 𝔓)) (𝔅 the centraliser of E in 𝔄, 𝔓 the radical) with π induced from Λ; or (b) π is induced from a representation Λ of F^×GL_n(O_F).

items.name: Lemma 10.7: case (b) supercuspidals are pure and ramified
items.statement: If π satisfies case (b) of Lemma 10.6, then π is pure; if moreover n ≥ 2 and q > 5, it is ramified (the lemma states both without these hypotheses): π ⊗ α ≅ π for α(g) = e^{2πi v(det g)/n}, so σ_π ≅ σ_π ⊗ ω (Genestier–Lafforgue, Remarque 0.2) with ω(Frob) = e^{2πi/n}, whence σ_π ≅ Ind_{W_{F_n}}^{W_F} χ for a character χ of the unramified degree-n extension; σ_π is pure, and ramified by Theorem 1.4(i).
items.note: Ramification comes from Theorem 1.4(i), which needs q > 5 and G not a torus; the lemma states neither (sourceIssues E2).

items.name: Lemma 10.8: the global intersection is a torus with repeated characters
items.statement: Let F = F_q((t)) and π as in case (a) of Lemma 10.6, with U_x standard maximal compact for x ≠ 0, ∞, U_0 = E^×J(β, 𝔄) and U_∞ the Iwahori-type subgroup of GL_n(F_q((t^{−1}))) opposite to 𝔄 whose diagonal blocks reduce into chosen Borel subgroups. For a suitable choice of these Borels, S = GL_n(F_q(t)) ∩ ∏_x U_x lies in a maximal torus of GL_n(F_q), and F_q^n restricted to S is a sum of n/k characters each repeated k times, for some divisor k > 1 of n.
items.note: Printed 'U_0 to be E^×(β, 𝔄)' (sourceIssues E10). The two cases are E/F ramified and E containing a residue field extension F_{q^k}.

items.name: Lemma 10.9: extending characters of S to the Iwahori subgroup at ∞
items.statement: If q > 2, every character of S extends to a nontrivial character of U_∞ (pulled back from (F_q^×)^n). If q > 3, every character of S extends to two such characters χ_a, χ_b, with χ_a trivial on at least one copy of F_q^× and χ_b trivial on none.

items.name: Proposition 10.10: supercuspidals of GL_n are ramified, and pure or wildly ramified
items.statement: Let n ≥ 2 and q the order of the residue field of F. As printed: if q > 2, every supercuspidal representation of GL(n, F) is ramified; if q > 3, every supercuspidal representation of GL(n, F) is either ramified and pure or wildly ramified. As proved: this holds for the supercuspidals of case (a) of Lemma 10.6 under those bounds, and for those of case (b) when q > 5.
items.note: Case (a) of Lemma 10.6 by Poincaré series with Lemmas 10.8–10.9; case (b) by Lemma 10.7, which rests on Theorem 1.4(i) and so needs q > 5 and n ≥ 2 (sourceIssues E2).

items.name: Corollary 10.11: supercuspidals of GL_n are not incorrigible
items.statement: For a supercuspidal representation π of GL(n, F) there is a tower of cyclic extensions as in (10.4) with BC_{F_r/F}(π) an irreducible constituent of an unramified principal series representation.
items.note: The key step of the proofs of the LLC for GL(n), obtained here from V. Lafforgue's parametrisation, Henniart–Lemaire base change and Bushnell–Kutzko types.

items.name: Definition 11.1: n-close local fields, and the depth of a parameter
items.statement: Local fields F (characteristic p) and F♯ (p-adic) are n-close if O_F/m_F^n ≅ O_{F♯}/m_{F♯}^n as rings. The depth of φ ∈ G^{ss}(G, F^?) is the least n with φ trivial on the upper-numbering ramification subgroup I^n_{F^?}; G^{ss,n}(G, F^?) is the set of parameters of depth at most n.
items.note: Printed 'the maximum n' (sourceIssues E11).

items.name: Theorem 11.2 (Deligne): close local fields have the same parameters of bounded depth
items.statement: (Deligne) If F and F♯ are n-close, there is a natural bijection G^{ss,n}(G, F) ≅ G^{ss,n}(G, F♯) (11.3).
items.note: EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.3 plans the comparison of close local fields for orbital integrals only; Deligne's Galois-side theorem is not planned.

items.name: Theorem 11.4 (Ganapathy–Kazhdan): Hecke algebras of close local fields
items.statement: (Kazhdan; Ganapathy) For G split and I_n(F^?) the n-th Iwahori filtration subgroup (the kernel of I(O) → I(O/m^n)), if F♯ and F are n-close there is a natural isomorphism H(G(F), I_n) ≅ H(G(F♯), I_n) (11.5) of finitely generated C-algebras and a bijection A_n(G, F) ≅ A_n(G, F♯) (11.6) of the representations generated by I_n-fixed vectors, with π^{I_n(F)} ≅ π♯^{I_n(F♯)} as modules under (11.5).

items.name: Fargues–Scholze semisimple parametrisation and Li Huerta's comparison
items.statement: (Fargues–Scholze) Every irreducible smooth representation of G over a p-adic (or equal-characteristic) local field has a semisimple L-parameter. (Li Huerta, arXiv:2301.09711) In equal characteristic it is compatible with V. Lafforgue's global parametrisation, hence equals the Genestier–Lafforgue parametrisation.
items.note: ES5 plans the Fargues–Scholze semisimple parameter assignment; GS.7 plans the local–global and equal-characteristic comparison.

items.name: Conjecture 11.7: Genestier–Lafforgue and Fargues–Scholze agree across close local fields
items.statement: For every n ≥ 1 the square formed by the Genestier–Lafforgue map A_n(G/F) → G^{ss,n}(G/F), the Fargues–Scholze map A_n(G/F♯) → G^{ss,n}(G/F♯), and the bijections (11.6) and (11.3) commutes.

items.name: Corollaries 11.8–11.9: consequences for p-adic groups
items.statement: Let F♯/Q_p have residue field k with |k| > 5, G split semisimple with p ∤ |W|, and assume Conjecture 11.7 for F♯ with an n-close F. (11.8) If σ ∈ A_n(G/F♯) is supercuspidal with pure Fargues–Scholze parameter L^{ss}(σ), then L^{ss}(σ) is ramified; more generally a pure σ ∈ A_n(G/F♯) with unramified parameter is a constituent of an unramified principal series. (11.9) Taking n = 1 (F = k((t)) is 1-close to F♯), every pure depth-zero supercuspidal of G(F♯) has ramified Fargues–Scholze parameter.
items.note: As printed, 11.8 omits σ ∈ A_n(G/F♯) (sourceIssues E12) and 11.9 says '0-close' (sourceIssues E13).

items.name: Questions 11.10–11.11
items.statement: Does the Fargues–Scholze parametrisation commute with the cyclic base change of §10.2? For F′/F♯ cyclic of prime order and π ∈ A_n(G/F♯), does every π′ in the base change of π lie in A_n(G/F′)?
items.note: Open questions, recorded for completeness.

items.name: Pseudo-coefficients of discrete series
items.statement: For a discrete series π_v of G(K_v) with central character ξ_v on Z^0(K_v), there is φ_{π_v} ∈ C_c^∞(G(K_v)/Z^0(K_v), ξ_v^{−1}) with Tr π′_v(φ_{π_v}) = 1 if π′_v ≅ π_v and 0 otherwise, for tempered irreducible π′_v with the same central character (trace Paley–Wiener, Bernstein–Deligne–Kazhdan); by the Langlands classification, Tr π′_v(φ_{π_v}) ≠ 0 for arbitrary irreducible π′_v forces π′_v to have the cuspidal support of π_v.

items.name: The Deligne–Kazhdan simple trace formula over function fields
items.statement: (Deligne–Kazhdan, [DKV, §A.1]) For f = ⊗_v f_v ∈ C_c^∞(G(A_K)/Z^0(A_K), ξ^{−1}) with a supercuspidal matrix coefficient at one place and supported, after G(A_K)-conjugation, only on regular elliptic elements of G(K): Σ_Π Tr Π(f) = Σ_δ ι(δ)^{−1} vol(G_δ(K)Z^0(A_K)∖G_δ(A_K)) O_δ(f) (A.2), both sums finite, over cuspidal Π with central character ξ and regular elliptic classes δ.
items.locator: Appendix A, proof of Lemma A.1, pp. 38–39

items.name: Lemma A.1 (Beuzart-Plessis): globalisation of discrete series up to cuspidal support
items.statement: Let S, S′ ⊂ |X| be disjoint with S′ ∩ S_ram = ∅; for v ∈ S let π_v be a discrete series with central character ξ_v on Z^0(K_v), at least one π_{v_0} supercuspidal; for v ∈ S′ let X_v ⊂ (T̂_v//W_v)_{ξ_v} be a proper Zariski-closed subset. Then there is a (cuspidal) automorphic Π with central character ξ such that Π_v has nonzero trace against a pseudo-coefficient of π_v for v ∈ S (so the same cuspidal support), and Π_v is unramified with Satake parameter outside X_v for v ∈ S′.
items.locator: Appendix A, Lemma A.1 and proof, pp. 38–39
items.note: The proof ends by citing condition '(iii)' where (iv) is meant (sourceIssues E14).

items.name: Lemma A.3: nonvanishing orbital integrals at a common regular elliptic element
items.statement: There are local test functions f_v (v ∈ S ∪ S′) satisfying (i)–(ii) and a regular elliptic δ ∈ G(K) with G^+_δ = G_δ and O_δ(f_v) ≠ 0 for every v ∈ S ∪ S′.
items.locator: Appendix A, Lemma A.3 and proof, p. 39
items.note: Uses Beuzart-Plessis's elliptic orthogonality for discrete series ([BP], a 2022 manuscript) and, when weak approximation fails, that the closure of G(K) in G(K_{S∪S′}) is open of finite index.

items.name: Elliptic orthogonality for discrete series (Beuzart-Plessis)
items.statement: (Beuzart-Plessis, [BP]) The Harish-Chandra characters of discrete series satisfy the elliptic orthogonality relations; in particular the elliptic regular orbital integrals of a pseudo-coefficient are not identically zero, even on a normal open subgroup of finite index.
items.locator: Appendix A, proof of Lemma A.3, p. 39
items.note: Cited as a manuscript (2022).

items.name: The closure of G(K) in finitely many completions has finite index
items.statement: (Platonov–Rapinchuk, proof of Prop. 7.9, valid in any characteristic) For a connected reductive G over a global field K and a finite set of places T, the closure of G(K) in ∏_{v∈T} G(K_v) is an open subgroup of finite index.
items.locator: Appendix A, proof of Lemma A.3, p. 39
items.note: AA.4 plans weak approximation in the cases a group theorem justifies, with its failures kept visible; this finite-index statement for function fields belongs there.

items.name: Automorphic forms and cuspidal spectrum over function fields; Satake; parabolic induction
items.statement: Cusp forms on G(K)∖G(A_K) with central character, the spectral decomposition of Poincaré series into cuspidal automorphic representations, Hecke operators and the unramified Satake parametrisation, parabolic induction, supercuspidal support and matrix-coefficient criteria.
items.note: FA.6 plans reductive-group automorphic forms over K; SR.2–SR.4 the local induction, supercuspidal support and Satake.
